title: Stage 4: Probes and resources
summary: Make the cluster understand when the API is healthy and how much it needs.

steps.title: Production settings
body: limits:   { memory: 512Mi }               # no CPU limit: avoid throttling
failureThreshold: 24                       # up to 2 minutes to start
httpGet: { path: /health/live, port: http }   # process only, no DB check
httpGet: { path: /health/ready, port: http }  # includes the DB check

steps.prompt: What QoS class do these API pods get?
steps.explain: Requests are set but do not equal limits (and there is no CPU limit), so Burstable.

steps.prompt: Complete the probes so a DB outage only takes pods out of rotation, never restarts them.
The startup probe runs every 5 s with `failureThreshold: 24`. How many seconds may the app take to start before it is restarted?

steps.title: Make the API production-ready
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl`; the current namespace is `todo`, and the manifests live in `~/k8s`. `todo-api` runs with no probes and no resources. Change the Deployment so that the `api` container has:
1. a **readiness** probe and a **liveness** probe, both `GET /health` on the port `http`;
2. a **startup** probe on the same endpoint, allowing up to 30 seconds (`failureThreshold` × `periodSeconds`);
3. requests of `100m` CPU and `64Mi` memory, and a memory limit of `128Mi`.
The rollout must finish with 2 ready pods.

checks.name: probes on /health
checks.cmd: kubectl get deploy todo-api -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.containers[0] | [.readinessProbe.httpGet.path, .livenessProbe.httpGet.path, .startupProbe.httpGet.path] | join(" ")'

checks.name: the startup probe allows 30 s
checks.cmd: kubectl get deploy todo-api -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].startupProbe | (.failureThreshold // 3) * (.periodSeconds // 10)'
checks.fail: `failureThreshold` × `periodSeconds` of the startup probe should be 30.

checks.name: 2 ready pods
checks.cmd: kubectl rollout status deploy/todo-api --timeout=40s >/dev/null; kubectl get deploy todo-api -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas} {.status.updatedReplicas}'
checks.fail: The rollout should finish with 2 ready, updated pods.

hints: Edit `~/k8s/deployment.yaml` and apply it, or `kubectl patch deploy todo-api` with a strategic merge patch naming the container `api`.
steps.explain: The startup probe protects slow starts (the liveness probe only begins once it has passed), readiness gates traffic, liveness restarts a hung process. Requests let the scheduler place the pod and protect it under pressure; a memory limit equal to (or a little above) the request keeps one leak from taking the node. In a real repo, change `~/k8s/deployment.yaml` too, so the file stays the source of truth.
